questions.text: Answer any seven questions from the following is short, preferably 1 or 2 sentence(s). What are the following?

subQuestions.text: Define the following and give one example of each:

Calculate the capillary effect in millimeters in a glass tube of $4\text{ mm}$ diameter, when immersed in (i) water and (ii) mercury. The temperature of the liquid is $20\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ and the values of surface tension of water and mercury at $20\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ in contact with air are $0.0735\text{ N/m}$ and $0.51\text{ N/m}$ respectively. The contact angle for water $= 0^\circ$ and for mercury $= 130^\circ$. Take specific weight of water at $20\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ as equal to $9790\text{ N/m}^3$.
State Newton's law of viscosity and distinguish between Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids with examples.

A cylinder of $120\text{ mm}$ diameter rotates concentrically inside a fixed cylinder of diameter $125\text{ mm}$. Both cylinders are $300\text{ mm}$ long. Find the viscosity of the liquid that fills the space between the cylinders if a torque of $0.90\text{ N m}$ is required to maintain a speed of $60\text{ r.p.m.}$
Define centre of buoyancy and metacentre. Explain stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium of a floating body.

A rectangular pontoon $12\text{ m}$ long and $8\text{ m}$ broad and $3\text{ m}$ deep weighs $800\text{ kN}$. It carries on its upper deck a boiler $5\text{ m}$ diameter weighing $500\text{ kN}$. The centre of gravity of the boiler and pontoon may be assumed as their centres of figure and on the same vertical line. Find the metacentric height. Weight of sea water is $10055\text{ N/m}^3$.
Define laminar flow, turbulent flow, give one example of each and distinguish between streamlines, streak lines and path line:

In a two-dimensional incompressible flow, the fluid velocity components are given by $u = x - 4y$ and $v = -y - 4x$. Show that velocity potential exists and determine its form. Find also the stream function.
State Buckingham's pi theorem. Explain how dimensionless constants can be framed from a set of variables influencing a phenomenon. What is the utility of Buckingham's theorem?

The discharge $Q$ over a weir depends on the head of water $H$, the acceleration due to gravity $g$, the density $\rho$, the viscosity $\mu$, and the surface tension $\sigma$. Obtain an expression for the discharge $Q$ using Buckingham's pi theorem.
What are the different energies of a fluid? Explain each of them.

A cylindrical tank $0.9\text{ m}$ in diameter and $2\text{ m}$ high open at top is filled with water to a depth of $1.5\text{ m}$. It is rotated about its vertical axis at $N\text{ r.p.m.}$ Determine the value of $N$ which will raise water level even with the brim.
Derive Darcy-Weisbach formula for calculating loss of head due to friction in a pipe.

A pipeline of $600\text{ mm}$ diameter is $1.5\text{ km}$ long. To increase the discharge another line of the same diameter is introduced parallel to the first in the second-half of the length. If $f = 0.01$ and head at inlet is $300\text{ mm}$, calculate the increase in discharge.
